changes.after: the Committee agreed today to increase policy accommodation by purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month.

changes.before: are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through late 2014.
changes.after: exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate are likely to be warranted at least through mid-2015.

If the outlook for the labor market does not improve substantially, the Committee will continue its purchases of agency mortgage-backed securities, undertake additional asset purchases, and employ its other policy tools as appropriate until such improvement is achieved in a context of price stability.
the Committee expects that a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy will remain appropriate for a considerable time after the economic recovery strengthens.

changes.before: The Committee expects economic growth to remain moderate over coming quarters and then to pick up very gradually.
changes.after: The Committee is concerned that, without further policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor market conditions.

changes.before: Inflation has declined since earlier this year, mainly reflecting lower prices of crude oil and gasoline, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.after: Inflation has been subdued, although the prices of some key commodities have increased recently.

changes.before: suggests that economic activity decelerated somewhat over the first half of this year.
changes.after: suggests that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace in recent months.

These actions, which together will increase the Committee’s holdings of longer-term securities by about $85 billion each month through the end of the year, should put downward pressure on longer-term interest rates

parsed.rationale: The Committee launched open-ended MBS purchases of $40 billion per month tied to substantial labor market improvement, extended rate guidance from late 2014 to mid-2015, and committed to staying accommodative after the recovery strengthens. Together these mark a clear dovish shift in policy that outweighs the slightly firmer description of activity and commodity prices.
